# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

This is a mild reminder, never a gate: in an unattended session, or when it would derail the work at hand, ignore it entirely and leave it for a later interactive session.

Give an `owner/name` (a fleet usually has one repo for this), or say "n/a — none" if this project has no such store. - product-wiki / product: What is the product — what does it do, and what is the core value it delivers? If the repo already carries a product brief or spec, read it and confirm rather than asking cold. - product-wiki / users: Who are the users or customers — the segments whose needs the research must track? [distill: recorded as intent; scopes the user-research wiki and whose problems the findings answer to]

I'm thinking that Claudinite's goal is "explonentially better your work", broken down as:
"your work" means "the things you work on", and not "all possible work", and also "the way you work", based on and automatically growing with your decisions and work patterns.
"exponential" means progressing, so there needs to be an automatic system to run growth, and run your work; but it also means "growing in a growing pace" which needs to have the growing corpus work predictably (not just hoping all rules apply) and not suffocate the context, so we built a system that grows prose into automatically generate linitng rules (giving predictability and frees context);
"automate" - grow automatically, execute verifiable work automatically, with a lightweight, verifyable task execution system; 
"your work" could mean one developer on one repo, one developer on a private fleet of repos, or an organization working in symphony on a fleet. Different flows, different mechanisms.
But to disseminate all relevant the knowledge automatically we had to have "packs", each with prose, linting rules, automatic tasks, autodiscovery mechanisms, and visibility (dashboarding).

On top of that, outside the claudinite core, the workflows I love are the executable-requirements, allowing the owner to work on testable, repeatable UI changes without the "build-deploy-run" loop, and let claude finish the loop by itself.

Consider how this framing changes the website. Render a new one. Deploy.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- site-visual-check: Screenshot and visually verify site/ (claudinite.com), desktop and mobile, and deliver the result to the owner. Use when changing site/ markup, CSS, or animations, or when checking responsive/mobile rendering.
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

message.content:
I'm thinking that Claudinite's goal is "explonentially better your work", broken down as:
"your work" means "the things you work on", and not "all possible work", and also "the way you work", based on and automatically growing with your decisions and work patterns.
"exponential" means progressing, so there needs to be an automatic system to run growth, and run your work; but it also means "growing in a growing pace" which needs to have the growing corpus work predictably (not just hoping all rules apply) and not suffocate the context, so we built a system that grows prose into automatically generate linitng rules (giving predictability and frees context);
"automate" - grow automatically, execute verifiable work automatically, with a lightweight, verifyable task execution system; 
"your work" could mean one developer on one repo, one developer on a private fleet of repos, or an organization working in symphony on a fleet. Different flows, different mechanisms.
But to disseminate all relevant the knowledge automatically we had to have "packs", each with prose, linting rules, automatic tasks, autodiscovery mechanisms, and visibility (dashboarding).

On top of that, outside the claudinite core, the workflows I love are the executable-requirements, allowing the owner to work on testable, repeatable UI changes without the "build-deploy-run" loop, and let claude finish the loop by itself.

Consider how this framing changes the website. Render a new one. Deploy.

1	# site/ — claudinite.com
2	
3	The static marketing site for Claudinite. No build step, no dependencies: the
4	directory is published as-is by [.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml](../.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml)
5	(GitHub Pages via the actions artifact flow) on every push to `main` — the
6	workflow carries no `paths:` filter, so a push that touches nothing under
7	`site/` still redeploys the same content.
8	
9	## Layout
10	
11	| Path | What it is | Who edits it |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| [index.html](index.html) | The one page: evergreen copy + the four mechanism explainers. Copy is deliberately terse — a claim earns its words or goes | Rarely — structure and evergreen claims |
14	| [assets/style.css](assets/style.css) | The whole design system (tokens at the top) | Rarely |
15	| [assets/main.js](assets/main.js) | Animations + rendering of the promoted-content slots | Rarely |
16	| [assets/analytics.js](assets/analytics.js) | Cookieless Cloudflare Web Analytics loader; no-ops until the deploy injects the token | Never — the token comes from the `CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN` repo variable |
17	| [privacy.html](privacy.html) | The privacy disclosure the analytics behaviour requires | When what the site collects changes — same commit as the change |
18	| [data/promoted.js](data/promoted.js) | **The promoted content: stats and the spotlight** | **Every promo refresh — edit this, usually nothing else** |
19	
20	## Updating promoted content (the expected frequent, agentic change)
21	
22	`data/promoted.js` is the single file a routine promo run edits. Contract:
23	
24	- **Truthful and verifiable.** Every stat, count, and update must be checkable
25	  against the vendored canon packs in this repo or against its history. No
26	  aspirational numbers, no invented dates.
27	- **`spotlight`** — the 3–5 benefits currently being promoted, ordered; the
28	  first entry renders full-width (visual priority). Taglines ≤ 90 chars.
29	  Benefits, never named packs: the page shows *how many* packs there are (the
30	  `pack-field` graphic and the `stats` count) and never *which*, so no copy
31	  goes stale when the canon's pack set moves.
32	- **`canonRef`** — keep in step with the `ref` stamp in
33	  [../.claudinite-checks.json](../.claudinite-checks.json) (short form).
34	- Keep the file a plain script (`window.CLAUDINITE = {...}`) — it must run
35	  from `file://` with no module loader.
36	
37	Evergreen sections (hero, mechanisms, adopt, FAQ) state how Claudinite works;
38	change them only when the product's mechanisms actually change.
39	
40	## The footer's version tooltip
41	
42	Every page's footer copyright carries the released version in its `title`, so a
43	visitor can name the build they are looking at. It is **generated**:
44	[scripts/bump-version.mjs](../scripts/bump-version.mjs) writes `package.json`
45	and stamps the pages in one run, and the deploy commits both — so never hand-edit
46	it. `node scripts/bump-version.mjs --stamp-only` repairs a drifted stamp without

# site/ — claudinite.com

The static marketing site for Claudinite. No build step, no dependencies: the
directory is published as-is by [.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml](../.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml)
(GitHub Pages via the actions artifact flow) on every push to `main` — the
workflow carries no `paths:` filter, so a push that touches nothing under
`site/` still redeploys the same content.

## Layout

| Path | What it is | Who edits it |
|---|---|---|
| [index.html](index.html) | The one page: evergreen copy + the four mechanism explainers. Copy is deliberately terse — a claim earns its words or goes | Rarely — structure and evergreen claims |
| [assets/style.css](assets/style.css) | The whole design system (tokens at the top) | Rarely |
| [assets/main.js](assets/main.js) | Animations + rendering of the promoted-content slots | Rarely |
| [assets/analytics.js](assets/analytics.js) | Cookieless Cloudflare Web Analytics loader; no-ops until the deploy injects the token | Never — the token comes from the `CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN` repo variable |
| [privacy.html](privacy.html) | The privacy disclosure the analytics behaviour requires | When what the site collects changes — same commit as the change |
| [data/promoted.js](data/promoted.js) | **The promoted content: stats and the spotlight** | **Every promo refresh — edit this, usually nothing else** |

## Updating promoted content (the expected frequent, agentic change)

`data/promoted.js` is the single file a routine promo run edits. Contract:

- **Truthful and verifiable.** Every stat, count, and update must be checkable
  against the vendored canon packs in this repo or against its history. No
  aspirational numbers, no invented dates.
- **`spotlight`** — the 3–5 benefits currently being promoted, ordered; the
  first entry renders full-width (visual priority). Taglines ≤ 90 chars.
  Benefits, never named packs: the page shows *how many* packs there are (the
  `pack-field` graphic and the `stats` count) and never *which*, so no copy
  goes stale when the canon's pack set moves.
- **`canonRef`** — keep in step with the `ref` stamp in
  [../.claudinite-checks.json](../.claudinite-checks.json) (short form).
- Keep the file a plain script (`window.CLAUDINITE = {...}`) — it must run
  from `file://` with no module loader.

Evergreen sections (hero, mechanisms, adopt, FAQ) state how Claudinite works;
change them only when the product's mechanisms actually change.

## The footer's version tooltip

Every page's footer copyright carries the released version in its `title`, so a
visitor can name the build they are looking at. It is **generated**:
[scripts/bump-version.mjs](../scripts/bump-version.mjs) writes `package.json`
and stamps the pages in one run, and the deploy commits both — so never hand-edit
it. `node scripts/bump-version.mjs --stamp-only` repairs a drifted stamp without
consuming a version number, and the
`claudinite-website/site-version-tooltip` check fails the build when the two
disagree.

`assets/analytics.js` keeps its own placeholder,
`REPLACE_WITH_CLOUDFLARE_WEB_ANALYTICS_TOKEN`, substituted at deploy time — see
the table above.

## Example repositories

This repository is private, so it can never be the site's "see a repo running
it" example. The link points at a public member of the fleet
([GoogleCalendarEventCreator](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator));
check any replacement is public before linking it.

## Local preview

Open `index.html` directly, or `python3 -m http.server -d site` and browse
`http://localhost:8000`.

## Custom domain

The Pages artifact flow takes its domain from the repository's Pages settings
(no `CNAME` file needed). When claudinite.com is connected there, the
`<link rel="canonical">` in `index.html` is already correct.

10	## Serve it
11	
12	```
13	(python3 -m http.server 8321 -d site >/dev/null 2>&1 &) && sleep 1
14	```

16	Kill the server once the last shot is taken; don't leave it running for the rest
17	of the session.

20	
21	`chrome --headless --screenshot` is fine **for desktop widths**:
22	
23	```

25	  --no-sandbox --window-size=1440,8400 --virtual-time-budget=8000 \
26	  --hide-scrollbars --screenshot=$SP/full.png "http://localhost:8321/"

30	animations, or sections render mid-transition and look broken when they aren't.
31	A full-page PNG is too tall to read in one go — crop it into sections with

35	
36	**Footgun, and it costs a whole phantom bug hunt.** A narrow
37	`--window-size=390,9500` headless shot renders the page at a *clamped* width and
38	crops content at the right edge. That looks exactly like a horizontal-overflow
39	bug across every section, and it is not one — the layout is fine at a real 390px
40	viewport. Don't start instrumenting CSS to find the "offender."
41

43

46	const b = await chromium.launch({
47	  executablePath: '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome',
48	  args: ['--no-sandbox'],
49	});
50	const p = await b.newPage({ viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 },
51	                            deviceScaleFactor: 2 });
52	await p.goto('http://localhost:8321/', { waitUntil: 'networkidle' });
53	await p.screenshot({ path: 'mobile.png', fullPage: true });
54	await b.close();
55	```

name: site-visual-check
description: Screenshot and visually verify site/ (claudinite.com), desktop and mobile, and deliver the result to the owner. Use when changing site/ markup, CSS, or animations, or when checking responsive/mobile rendering.
---

The site is static and dependency-free, so verification is: serve `site/`, render it
in a real browser, look at the image. Do that on **every** change to `site/` — the
page is iterated frequently and unreviewed.

## Serve it

```
(python3 -m http.server 8321 -d site >/dev/null 2>&1 &) && sleep 1
```

Kill the server once the last shot is taken; don't leave it running for the rest
of the session.

## Desktop shots

`chrome --headless --screenshot` is fine **for desktop widths**:

```
/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome --headless --disable-gpu \
  --no-sandbox --window-size=1440,8400 --virtual-time-budget=8000 \
  --hide-scrollbars --screenshot=$SP/full.png "http://localhost:8321/"
```

`--virtual-time-budget` must outlast the reveal-on-scroll and mechanism
animations, or sections render mid-transition and look broken when they aren't.
A full-page PNG is too tall to read in one go — crop it into sections with
Pillow before viewing.

## Mobile — do NOT use `--window-size` to fake a phone viewport

**Footgun, and it costs a whole phantom bug hunt.** A narrow
`--window-size=390,9500` headless shot renders the page at a *clamped* width and
crops content at the right edge. That looks exactly like a horizontal-overflow
bug across every section, and it is not one — the layout is fine at a real 390px
viewport. Don't start instrumenting CSS to find the "offender."

For any width below desktop, drive a real browser context instead:

```js
import { chromium } from 'playwright-core';  // npm i playwright-core in scratch
const b = await chromium.launch({
  executablePath: '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome',
  args: ['--no-sandbox'],
});
const p = await b.newPage({ viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 },
                            deviceScaleFactor: 2 });
await p.goto('http://localhost:8321/', { waitUntil: 'networkidle' });
await p.screenshot({ path: 'mobile.png', fullPage: true });
await b.close();
```

`newContext`/`newPage` with an explicit `viewport` is what actually applies the
media queries; the CLI flag does not.

## Show the owner

A raw full-page capture is rejected as too large — downscale to roughly 600–720px
wide and send it as JPEG (quality ~82), alongside a full-size hero crop.

1	# Product requirements
2	
3	The human-reviewed distillation of the `product-wiki/` research into product
4	requirements. Never auto-grown — a wiki finding that should move a requirement
5	gets a growth-log note and waits for a human to land it here.
6	
7	## Status: proposed first distillation (2026-07-31, pending owner review)
8	
9	This set was derived on explicit owner instruction at the end of the
10	2026-07-31 ecosystem research pass, and lands through that pass's pull
11	request — the owner's review of that PR is the human gate this sink
12	requires. Until the PR is merged by the owner, everything below is
13	*proposed*, not accepted. Each requirement traces to the research page(s)
14	that motivate it; none of the wiki pages may be cited by the rest of the
15	repo — this page is the only crossing point.
16	
17	### Product mechanics
18	
19	- **R1 — Tenant canon.** Make the canon location configurable (org-owned,
20	  private canons in the customer's own tenancy); remove the hard-coded
21	  personal public repo and owner-affiliation fleet enumeration. Motivated by:
22	  Positioning gap 1; enterprise requirement #3 (Customers).
23	- **R2 — Multi-agent surface.** Emit AGENTS.md (and optionally Cursor/Copilot
24	  files) from pack rules so non-Claude agents at least read the conventions;
25	  keep SKILL.md-standard skills as the interchange format. Claude Code
26	  remains the enforced first-class target — this is emission, not parity.
27	  Motivated by: enterprise near-blocker #2 (Customers); AGENTS.md format
28	  convergence (Market).
29	- **R3 — Pinning, channels, rollback.** Replace track-canon-head with
30	  pinnable corpus versions, at least stable/head channels, and a rollback
31	  path; keep bot-opened update PRs as the drift mechanism. Motivated by:
32	  every winning comparable shipped pins + bot PRs (Methods); Positioning
33	  gap 3.
34	- **R4 — True one-command adopt.** Close the gap between "one conversation
35	  to adopt" and reality: vendored bootstrap, and a documented or automated
36	  path for provisioning the executor routines that agentic dispatches
37	  depend on. Motivated by: zero-effort adoption as a winner trait (Methods);
38	  Positioning gaps 6 and 9.
39	- **R5 — Fleet status surface.** A minimal aggregation view (even a
40	  generated markdown/JSON roll-up in the canon repo) answering "is the fleet
41	  converged and passing?" per repo — the champion's ROI slide and the
42	  scorecard-educated buyer's expectation. Motivated by: Positioning gap 5;
43	  enterprise requirement #5 (Customers); consider feeding existing scorecard
44	  products (Cortex/Port) instead of building a dashboard (Positioning open
45	  question).
46	
47	### Commercial
48	
49	- **R6 — Model: free-for-OSS + paid ongoing loop.** Free for public repos;
50	  price the ongoing stream, not the files — hosted convergence/maintenance
51	  operation, private canon/packs, and (for enterprise) SLA. Indicative

# Product requirements

The human-reviewed distillation of the `product-wiki/` research into product
requirements. Never auto-grown — a wiki finding that should move a requirement
gets a growth-log note and waits for a human to land it here.

## Status: proposed first distillation (2026-07-31, pending owner review)

This set was derived on explicit owner instruction at the end of the
2026-07-31 ecosystem research pass, and lands through that pass's pull
request — the owner's review of that PR is the human gate this sink
requires. Until the PR is merged by the owner, everything below is
*proposed*, not accepted. Each requirement traces to the research page(s)
that motivate it; none of the wiki pages may be cited by the rest of the
repo — this page is the only crossing point.

### Product mechanics

- **R1 — Tenant canon.** Make the canon location configurable (org-owned,
  private canons in the customer's own tenancy); remove the hard-coded
  personal public repo and owner-affiliation fleet enumeration. Motivated by:
  Positioning gap 1; enterprise requirement #3 (Customers).
- **R2 — Multi-agent surface.** Emit AGENTS.md (and optionally Cursor/Copilot
  files) from pack rules so non-Claude agents at least read the conventions;
  keep SKILL.md-standard skills as the interchange format. Claude Code
  remains the enforced first-class target — this is emission, not parity.
  Motivated by: enterprise near-blocker #2 (Customers); AGENTS.md format
  convergence (Market).
- **R3 — Pinning, channels, rollback.** Replace track-canon-head with
  pinnable corpus versions, at least stable/head channels, and a rollback
  path; keep bot-opened update PRs as the drift mechanism. Motivated by:
  every winning comparable shipped pins + bot PRs (Methods); Positioning
  gap 3.
- **R4 — True one-command adopt.** Close the gap between "one conversation
  to adopt" and reality: vendored bootstrap, and a documented or automated
  path for provisioning the executor routines that agentic dispatches
  depend on. Motivated by: zero-effort adoption as a winner trait (Methods);
  Positioning gaps 6 and 9.
- **R5 — Fleet status surface.** A minimal aggregation view (even a
  generated markdown/JSON roll-up in the canon repo) answering "is the fleet
  converged and passing?" per repo — the champion's ROI slide and the
  scorecard-educated buyer's expectation. Motivated by: Positioning gap 5;
  enterprise requirement #5 (Customers); consider feeding existing scorecard
  products (Cortex/Port) instead of building a dashboard (Positioning open
  question).

### Commercial

- **R6 — Model: free-for-OSS + paid ongoing loop.** Free for public repos;
  price the ongoing stream, not the files — hosted convergence/maintenance
  operation, private canon/packs, and (for enterprise) SLA. Indicative
  bands from anchors: $10–40/seat/mo or pre-commit.ci-style flat org tiers
  ($20–100/mo band), with behavioral seat definitions ("devs whose repos
  consume a pack"). A one-time entry SKU for indies ($29–79) is compatible
  with the evidence. Motivated by: Business (scarcity analysis, anchors);
  Customers (per-segment willingness to pay).
- **R7 — Procurement package.** A written data-flow story (what leaves the
  customer's repos: nothing; what credentials the bots hold and why), a
  supply-chain provenance story for the vendored canon, and a security-review
  FAQ. SOC 2 only becomes relevant when a hosted component exists. Motivated

input.title: Reframe the site around "exponentially better your work"
input.body:
The owner has restated Claudinite's positioning, and the site's current framing ("agent conventions with teeth" — enforcement-first) no longer leads with it. The new framing, verbatim in structure:

- **Goal: "exponentially better your work."** "Your work" = the things you work on (not all possible work) *and* the way you work, growing automatically from your decisions and work patterns.
- **"Exponential"** = progressing automatically (a system runs growth and runs your work), and growing at a *growing* pace — which requires the corpus to behave predictably (not hoping rules apply) and not suffocate the context: prose grows into automatically generated linting rules (checks), giving predictability and freeing context.
- **"Automate"** = grow automatically and execute verifiable work automatically, with a lightweight, verifiable task execution system.
- **Scales**: one developer on one repo, one developer on a private fleet, or an organization working in symphony on a fleet — different flows, different mechanisms.
- **Packs** are the dissemination unit: prose, linting rules, automatic tasks, autodiscovery, visibility.
- Outside the core: the **executable-requirements** workflow — testable, repeatable UI changes without the build-deploy-run loop; Claude finishes the loop itself.

Task: rewrite `site/index.html` (and whatever `site/README.md` self-descriptions the restructure falsifies) around this framing, keeping the design system, the data-driven promoted slots, and the mechanism animations where they still serve. Visually verify per `site-visual-check`, then deploy (merge to `main`; `deploy-pages.yml` publishes on push to `main`).

Why How Scale FAQ Adopt

A growth system for Claude Code

Your work, exponentially better.

Claudinite grows a corpus from the way you actually work — then enforces it with generated checks and runs the upkeep itself. Every session starts ahead of the last.

Adopt it in your repo The canon on GitHub

Plain files in your repo. No service, no account.

Why this exists

Agents don’t compound on their own.

“Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration.”

Claude Code docs, on CLAUDE.md

01 Amnesia

Every session starts from zero. Your decisions evaporate on exit.

02 No teeth

Nothing fails when a convention is ignored. So it is.

03 Suffocation

Pile the growing rulebook into context and it crowds out the work.

Compounding needs all three fixed: memory that grows, rules that bite, context left free. Claudinite is that system.

Mechanism 01 · grow

It grows from
your work

Not all possible work — yours: the things you work on, and the way you work on them, read from your own sessions and decisions.

  • Sessions are captured — friction, backtracks and calls you made become lessons.
  • Lessons land as local rules, in a PR you review.
  • The portable ones promote to the canon — and reach every repo you run.

Mechanism 02 · enforce

Predictable,
not hopeful

A rule the agent might apply is a hope. So prose is grown into generated checks — lint for how you work. They run when the agent tries to stop; the finding is the instruction.

  • Blocking findings hold the session open.
  • Advisory findings just surface.
  • The repo-facing ones run again in CI.

prose→ skill→ check

Each rung up adds certainty and frees context — the corpus keeps growing without suffocating the session.

claude — your-repo

◆ SessionStart · 3 packs loaded · rules injected

> implement the signup flow

… edits, commits, tries to end …

◆ Stop · running checks

✗ task-lifecycle blocking no commit references an issue

  fix: reference the task issue — e.g. “refs #42”

> git commit --amend -m "Add signup flow (refs #42)"

✓ 14 checks · all green — session ends clean

Mechanism 03 · automate

Work that
runs itself

Growth is scheduled, and so is the work: lightweight tasks the fleet executes unattended, each with a verifiable outcome.

  • Upkeep on the repo’s schedule — tidy sweeps, wiki growth, prose→check conversion.
  • Every repo re-vendors the canon nightly — no repo falls behind.
  • Every automated change is a PR, gated by your own CI.
canon @ 005edd2

nightly baselining · PR → CI → merge

Mechanism 04 · disseminate

The pack
carries it

Knowledge compounds only if it travels whole. A pack ships a practice with everything it needs to survive — and to be found.

  • Prose — every session, automatically.
  • Checks — the generated lint that enforces it.
  • Skills and tasks — procedure on demand, upkeep on schedule.
  • A manifest — discoverable in the catalog, adopted by interview, visible per repo.
RULES.mdevery session

Always loaded.

checks/*.mjsblockingadvisory

The finding names the fix.

skills/on demand

Procedure, on demand.

tasks/scheduled

Upkeep the repo runs on itself.

pack.mjsvisibility

Declares itself: catalog entry, adoption interview, a badge per repo.

Who it’s for

One repo. A fleet. An organization.

01 One developer, one repo

The session loop alone: your repo gets stricter and smarter every time you work it.

02 One developer, a fleet

A private canon: a lesson paid for in one repo reaches all of them by morning.

03 An organization

Teams in symphony: shared packs carry how the org works, and every repo visibly keeps up.

Different flows, different mechanisms — one compounding loop.

Beyond the core

Requirements
you can execute

The workflow this buys: state a UI change as a requirement, and the agent finishes the build-run-verify loop against it — repeatably, without you driving it.

  • The requirement becomes an executable spec — a test that fails first.
  • Claude runs the loop: change, build, verify — again, until it passes.
  • You review a change that already proved itself.
claude — your-app

> the signup button stays disabled until the form validates

◆ requirement recorded → executable spec

✗ spec fails: button enabled on empty form

… edit · rebuild · re-run the spec …

✓ spec passes — change ready for review

In the canon now

What ships today

Adopt

One conversation,
then one wire-up

  1. Point Claude Code at the canon. “Adopt Claudinite — follow missingbulb/Claudinite’s bootstrap.md.”
  2. Answer the interview. It vendors the canon, wires the hooks, scheduler and CI — one green PR.
  3. Merge, then wire the runner once — an endpoint and a token. After that it runs itself.
Get Claudinite See a repo running it
  • No server, no account.
  • Works alongside your CLAUDE.md.
  • Every automated change is a PR.
claude — acme/payments

$ claude

>

◆ fetching canon · running the adoption interview…

✓ canon vendored at .claudinite/shared/ (ref 005edd2)

✓ packs declared · interview answered

✓ hooks registered · scheduler wired (minute :26) · CI sweep added

✓ conformance sweep green — bootstrap PR opened

FAQ

Fair questions

What gets added to my repo?

A vendored canon, a declaration, hooks, a scheduler workflow and a CI step — one PR.

Do I have to write the rules myself?

No. Most arrive as lessons mined from your own sessions; you review the PRs that land them.

Will it fight my CLAUDE.md?

No. It adds the layer that file can’t carry, and keeps it lean.

What happens when a check fails?

It holds the session open and states the fix. Repo-facing checks run again on every PR.

Which agents does it support?

Claude Code today. Other agents keep reading your CLAUDE.md.

How do I leave?

Delete .claudinite/, its hook entries, the scheduler workflow and the CI step.

claudinite

Your work, compounding.

Canon repository Mechanisms Adopt Privacy

Built by an agent session governed by Claudinite’s own checks.

© 2026 MissingBulb

# site/ — claudinite.com

The static marketing site for Claudinite. No build step, no dependencies: the
directory is published as-is by [.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml](../.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml)
(GitHub Pages via the actions artifact flow) on every push to `main` — the
workflow carries no `paths:` filter, so a push that touches nothing under
`site/` still redeploys the same content.

## Layout

| Path | What it is | Who edits it |
|---|---|---|
| [index.html](index.html) | The one page: evergreen copy + the four mechanism explainers. Copy is deliberately terse — a claim earns its words or goes | Rarely — structure and evergreen claims |
| [assets/style.css](assets/style.css) | The whole design system (tokens at the top) | Rarely |
| [assets/main.js](assets/main.js) | Animations + rendering of the promoted-content slots | Rarely |
| [assets/analytics.js](assets/analytics.js) | Cookieless Cloudflare Web Analytics loader; no-ops until the deploy injects the token | Never — the token comes from the `CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN` repo variable |
| [privacy.html](privacy.html) | The privacy disclosure the analytics behaviour requires | When what the site collects changes — same commit as the change |
| [data/promoted.js](data/promoted.js) | **The promoted content: stats and the spotlight** | **Every promo refresh — edit this, usually nothing else** |

## Updating promoted content (the expected frequent, agentic change)

`data/promoted.js` is the single file a routine promo run edits. Contract:

- **Truthful and verifiable.** Every stat, count, and update must be checkable
  against the vendored canon packs in this repo or against its history. No
  aspirational numbers, no invented dates.
- **`spotlight`** — the 3–5 benefits currently being promoted, ordered; the
  first entry renders full-width (visual priority). Taglines ≤ 90 chars.
  Benefits, never named packs: the page shows *how many* packs there are (the
  `pack-field` graphic and the `stats` count) and never *which*, so no copy
  goes stale when the canon's pack set moves.
- **`canonRef`** — keep in step with the `ref` stamp in
  [../.claudinite-checks.json](../.claudinite-checks.json) (short form).
- Keep the file a plain script (`window.CLAUDINITE = {...}`) — it must run
  from `file://` with no module loader.

Evergreen sections (hero, mechanisms, adopt, FAQ) state how Claudinite works;
change them only when the product's mechanisms actually change.

## The footer's version tooltip

Every page's footer copyright carries the released version in its `title`, so a
visitor can name the build they are looking at. It is **generated**:
[scripts/bump-version.mjs](../scripts/bump-version.mjs) writes `package.json`
and stamps the pages in one run, and the deploy commits both — so never hand-edit
it. `node scripts/bump-version.mjs --stamp-only` repairs a drifted stamp without
consuming a version number, and the
`claudinite-website/site-version-tooltip` check fails the build when the two
disagree.

`assets/analytics.js` keeps its own placeholder,
`REPLACE_WITH_CLOUDFLARE_WEB_ANALYTICS_TOKEN`, substituted at deploy time — see
the table above.

## Example repositories

This repository is private, so it can never be the site's "see a repo running
it" example. The link points at a public member of the fleet
([GoogleCalendarEventCreator](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator));
check any replacement is public before linking it.

## Local preview

Open `index.html` directly, or `python3 -m http.server -d site` and browse
`http://localhost:8000`.

## Custom domain

The Pages artifact flow takes its domain from the repository's Pages settings
(no `CNAME` file needed). When claudinite.com is connected there, the
`<link rel="canonical">` in `index.html` is already correct.

input.body:
Closes #253

Rewrites `site/index.html` from the enforcement-first framing ("agent conventions with teeth") to the owner's compounding framing:

- **Hero**: "Your work, exponentially better." — grows a corpus from the way you work, enforces it with generated checks, runs the upkeep itself.
- **Why**: the three failure modes that stop agents compounding — amnesia, no teeth, context suffocation — with the same Claude Code docs citation.
- **Mechanisms reframed as grow → enforce → automate → disseminate**: the growth loop leads; the session-terminal section now carries the prose→skill→check ladder ("predictable, not hopeful"); the baselining board carries the verifiable-task/automation story; the pack anatomy gains a fifth `pack.mjs` layer (catalog entry, adoption interview, badge per repo).
- **New "scale" section**: one developer/one repo, one developer/a fleet, an organization in symphony.
- **New "beyond the core" section**: the executable-requirements workflow, with a static terminal showing a requirement becoming an executable spec the agent iterates against.
- Canon stats/spotlight slots, adopt flow, FAQ (one new entry), and all animation JS untouched; footer tagline now "Your work, compounding."

Supporting changes: a `reveal` delay tier for the fifth pack layer and a contrast fix for the promotion ladder on the dark section (`site/assets/style.css`); `site/README.md`'s description of the page updated to match the new structure.

Verified: the two local pack test files pass (20/20), and the page was rendered and visually checked at 1440px and a real 390px viewport (screenshots delivered in the session; the hero-wrap collision and the invisible dark-section ladder chip found there are fixed in this diff).

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

file.content:
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Dispatchable so baselining can start this run on the nightly maintenance PR.
  # That PR's branch push and its open both ride the Action's GITHUB_TOKEN, and
  # GitHub's recursion guard suppresses workflow runs for events that token
  # authors — so the PR gets no pull_request run at all, and `maintenance.delivery:
  # auto-merge` waits on a check that never appears. workflow_dispatch is the
  # guard's one documented exception, which is why baselining's deliver() starts
  # the checks itself.
  workflow_dispatch:
jobs:
  conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Claudinite world-scope conformance sweep
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs
      # The glob is explicit on purpose: bare `node --test` skips dot-directories,
      # so it would find none of these and still exit green (claudinite-website/node-test-discovery).
      - name: Local pack rule fixtures
        run: node --test '.claudinite/local/packs/**/*.test.mjs'

* Stop naming packs and this private repo; version in the footer (refs #235)

This repository is private, so it can't be the site's example: the "see a
consumer repo" CTA and the footer link both pointed here. The CTA now
points at a public member of the fleet, and the footer link is gone.

No individual packs anywhere on the page — no per-pack cards, no pack
names, no check/skill/task names. A field of pack glyphs with a handful
lit carries what actually matters (there are many; you declare the ones
you want), and dates only when the count changes. The dated `updates`
feed goes with them.

The footer reads "© 2026 MissingBulb" and carries the released version in
its title tooltip, substituted into the artifact at deploy time from the
same bump the release performs.

Another ~90 words out; visible prose is down to ~536.

Verified at 1440px and at a real 390px viewport (zero horizontal
overflow), the deploy's version substitution proved against a copy of the
page, and world-scope checks green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KDTqRVGQtKWy4i1SCRUMM9

* Guard the footer's version with a check, not a deploy substitution (refs #235)

The tooltip's number was substituted into the artifact at deploy time, so
the repo itself never carried it and nothing could verify it. Now the
version is a generated copy in the pages, and a blocking check is its
drift guard.

- scripts/bump-version.mjs owns both sides: it writes package.json and
  stamps every page carrying the footer copyright, in one run.
  `--stamp-only` repairs drift without consuming a version number.
- claudinite-website/site-version-tooltip fails when a page's stamp
  disagrees with package.json, is missing, or is still the placeholder.
  Seen red first against the real tree on both pages.
- The deploy loses its sed step; its commit now stages the pages beside
  package.json, so main stays self-consistent after a release.

Fixtures cover drift, a missing stamp, the placeholder, pages without the
footer, html outside site/, and an unreadable package.json.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KDTqRVGQtKWy4i1SCRUMM9

* Website wiki becomes competitor-marketing research (refs #235)

The page was a log of our own site decisions living in a research tree.
Decisions about our own product are requirements, so they move to the
human-reviewed sink as R11–R14 (headline and the vendor quotation; what
the page may not name; terse by construction; the version tooltip), and
the page is re-scoped to what rivals and adjacent vendors actually say.

Fresh copy research landed with the re-scope: Ruler and ai-rulez READMEs
read directly. ai-rulez is the find — it markets a builtin
"ai-governance" domain whose bullets read like enforcement, but its own
definition of a domain is rule text injected into configs, and its
`verify` is scoped to committed output matching its sources. The
vocabulary is being taken; the mechanism isn't.

rulesync.dev's live copy stays unverified: the domain is egress-blocked
here, and that is recorded as needing a human rather than a later pass.

Cross-references in the wiki index and Positioning follow the new scope.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KDTqRVGQtKWy4i1SCRUMM9

* Research pass: the vendor now states the enforcement premise (refs #233)

Three primary-source findings ahead of the site messaging rewrite:

- Anthropic's memory doc says CLAUDE.md is "context, not enforced
  configuration" and points at hooks for anything that must block. The
  category's blind spot is now vendor-stated rather than argued.
- claude-code#6235 (AGENTS.md, 4,944 👍) closed `completed` on 2026-08-17
  while the docs still say Claude Code does not read the file — the answer
  shipped was `/import`, a one-time copy. The interop whitespace is durable
  by decision, not backlog.
- Auto memory is documented machine-local and never shared, so nothing
  native promotes a lesson beyond one machine.

Ruler's README re-read the same day: still distribution plus file-drift,
so "they check the rules arrived; we check they were followed" holds.

Positioning distils the benefits to three — rules that bite, a fleet that
converges itself, lessons that travel.

* Refocus the site on three benefits and cut ~38% of the prose (refs #233)

Headline moves from the copy-paste pain (which the rule-sync category
sells the fix for) to the enforcement gap, and Anthropic's own sentence —
"Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration" — leads the
Why section as the page's only quotation.

Every mechanism keeps its animation and heading and loses its explanatory
paragraph; bullets are fragments. Visible prose drops from ~1,000 to ~620
words. The promoted spotlight names benefits rather than features.

Retires the four attackable claims: CI runs the repo-facing checks (not
"the same sweep"), the leave story lists all four artifacts, adoption is
"one conversation, then one wire-up" with the manual runner step named,
and the page says Claude Code rather than "AI coding agents".

Also corrects the deploy self-description in site/README.md and the
workflow header: there is no `paths:` filter, so every push to main
redeploys.

Converts the deploy-trigger clause of claudinite-website RULES.md rule 1
("a behaviour change must correct every self-description it falsifies, in
the same commit") into claudinite-website/deploy-trigger-claims (blocking).
Prose claiming the Pages deploy is path-filtered must be backed by an
actual paths:/paths-ignore: list on deploy-pages.yml's parsed on.push
trigger; an unqualified "publishes on every push to main" is never judged.

It fired on the live tree at three surfaces still claiming the #45
paths: filter after it was dropped: deploy-pages.yml's own header,
site/README.md, and product-wiki/Website/README.md (whose gerund
phrasing "touching site/**", with no "that", needed a QUALIFIER
alternative the earlier attempts at this check missed). All three are
corrected in this commit to the actual unfiltered trigger.

RULES.md rule 1 stays whole (deletion test): the check covers only the

* Stop naming packs and this private repo; version in the footer (refs #235)

This repository is private, so it can't be the site's example: the "see a
consumer repo" CTA and the footer link both pointed here. The CTA now
points at a public member of the fleet, and the footer link is gone.

No individual packs anywhere on the page — no per-pack cards, no pack

The footer reads "© 2026 MissingBulb" and carries the released version in

same bump the release performs.

Another ~90 words out; visible prose is down to ~536.

* Guard the footer's version with a check, not a deploy substitution (refs #235)

The tooltip's number was substituted into the artifact at deploy time, so
the repo itself never carried it and nothing could verify it. Now the
version is a generated copy in the pages, and a blocking check is its
drift guard.

- scripts/bump-version.mjs owns both sides: it writes package.json and
  stamps every page carrying the footer copyright, in one run.
  `--stamp-only` repairs drift without consuming a version number.
- claudinite-website/site-version-tooltip fails when a page's stamp
  disagrees with package.json, is missing, or is still the placeholder.
  Seen red first against the real tree on both pages.
- The deploy loses its sed step; its commit now stages the pages beside
  package.json, so main stays self-consistent after a release.

Fixtures cover drift, a missing stamp, the placeholder, pages without the
footer, html outside site/, and an unreadable package.json.

* Website wiki becomes competitor-marketing research (refs #235)

The page was a log of our own site decisions living in a research tree.
Decisions about our own product are requirements, so they move to the
human-reviewed sink as R11–R14 (headline and the vendor quotation; what
the page may not name; terse by construction; the version tooltip), and
the page is re-scoped to what rivals and adjacent vendors actually say.

Fresh copy research landed with the re-scope: Ruler and ai-rulez READMEs
read directly. ai-rulez is the find — it markets a builtin
"ai-governance" domain whose bullets read like enforcement, but its own
definition of a domain is rule text injected into configs, and its
`verify` is scoped to committed output matching its sources. The
vocabulary is being taken; the mechanism isn't.

rulesync.dev's live copy stays unverified: the domain is egress-blocked
here, and that is recorded as needing a human rather than a later pass.

Cross-references in the wiki index and Positioning follow the new scope.

* Research pass: the vendor now states the enforcement premise (refs #233)

Three primary-source findings ahead of the site messaging rewrite:

  configuration" and points at hooks for anything that must block. The
  category's blind spot is now vendor-stated rather than argued.
- claude-code#6235 (AGENTS.md, 4,944 👍) closed `completed` on 2026-08-17

  shipped was `/import`, a one-time copy. The interop whitespace is durable
  by decision, not backlog.
- Auto memory is documented machine-local and never shared, so nothing
  native promotes a lesson beyond one machine.

Ruler's README re-read the same day: still distribution plus file-drift,
so "they check the rules arrived; we check they were followed" holds.

Positioning distils the benefits to three — rules that bite, a fleet that
converges itself, lessons that travel.

sells the fix for) to the enforcement gap, and Anthropic's own sentence —
"Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration" — leads the
Why section as the page's only quotation.

Every mechanism keeps its animation and heading and loses its explanatory
paragraph; bullets are fragments. Visible prose drops from ~1,000 to ~620
words. The promoted spotlight names benefits rather than features.

Retires the four attackable claims: CI runs the repo-facing checks (not
"the same sweep"), the leave story lists all four artifacts, adoption is
"one conversation, then one wire-up" with the manual runner step named,
and the page says Claude Code rather than "AI coding agents".

workflow header: there is no `paths:` filter, so every push to main
redeploys.

Converts the deploy-trigger clause of claudinite-website RULES.md rule 1
("a behaviour change must correct every self-description it falsifies, in
the same commit") into claudinite-website/deploy-trigger-claims (blocking).
Prose claiming the Pages deploy is path-filtered must be backed by an
actual paths:/paths-ignore: list on deploy-pages.yml's parsed on.push
trigger; an unqualified "publishes on every push to main" is never judged.

It fired on the live tree at three surfaces still claiming the #45
paths: filter after it was dropped: deploy-pages.yml's own header,
site/README.md, and product-wiki/Website/README.md (whose gerund
phrasing "touching site/**", with no "that", needed a QUALIFIER
alternative the earlier attempts at this check missed). All three are
corrected in this commit to the actual unfiltered trigger.

RULES.md rule 1 stays whole (deletion test): the check covers only the

- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. - writing-migration-plans: How to order the phases of an implementation or migration plan so nothing stalls mid-run — front-load the out-of-band setup, collapse the review gates into one stacked-PR pass, leave only executable steps — and how to keep its tracking issue append-only while implementing.
